title: Container Bookings: Freight, Surcharge and Premium Billing
content:
This page describes how ocean freight and the charges that travel with it are billed to a Container Bookings booking.

## Policy clause

Freight is billed when a booking is confirmed, and billed again for any containers that an amendment adds; each charge code is billed as an entry of its own. The ocean freight and terminal handling lines take their rate either from the spot quote the customer accepted or from the rate sheet filed under the referenced service contract. Either kind of rate can be booked only during the product's rate-life period, counted in calendar days from its issue; once that period has run out, a fresh quote is required.

Bunker cost follows the product's bunker setting. Under the contract-schedule setting, a separate bunker adjustment entry is billed from the contract's schedule. Under the included-in-quote setting, bunker cost has no line of its own, and adding one is not permitted.

The peak season surcharge equals the product's peak season rate multiplied by the number of containers being charged, and it is billed only when that rate is above 0.00. The equipment imbalance surcharge is formed in the same way from the product's imbalance rate. A product whose rate for either surcharge is 0.00 is exempt from it, and no entry is made. The loading guarantee premium is the product's premium rate multiplied by the containers being charged, billed when the rate is above 0.00. The manual booking fee is billed once for the booking, and only when the booking came in through the customer service desk and the product's fee is above 0.00.

Freight may be billed only while the booking's status is confirmed, equipment released or gated in, as the booking record shows. None of these lines, whether freight, surcharge, premium or manual booking fee, is ever eligible for a goodwill waiver.

## Charge lines at a glance

| Charge | Basis | Written when |
|---|---|---|
| Ocean freight, terminal handling | accepted quote or filed contract rate | at confirmation, and for containers added by amendment |
| Bunker adjustment | contract schedule | only under the contract-schedule setting |
| Peak season surcharge | rate multiplied by containers charged | rate above 0.00 |
| Equipment imbalance surcharge | rate multiplied by containers charged | rate above 0.00 |
| Loading guarantee premium | rate multiplied by containers charged | rate above 0.00 |
| Manual booking fee | flat, once per booking | desk channel and fee above 0.00 |

## Worked example (hypothetical rates)

Assume an invented product with a peak season rate of 90.00, an imbalance rate of 0.00 and a premium rate of 60.00, and a booking of 5 containers placed online. At confirmation the peak season surcharge is 450.00 and the premium is 300.00; no imbalance entry is made because the rate is 0.00, and no manual booking fee arises because the booking did not come through the desk. None of these rates belongs to an actual product.
